lines.english: "Good work on your paper."
"Your seminar's pretty strict, isn't it, Haruki-kun? I can't believe they're making you work almost all the way until the winter break."
"I still need to hand in assigned work every week, but they don't take more than a couple of hours, so I don't really have to deal with my seminar all that much right now."
"But honestly, the graduate thesis thing looks pretty daunting. There's always at least one person who fails to graduate each year. …I've gotta give it my all so I don't end up being that person."
"Speaking of which, have you decided on a topic for your thesis yet?"
"This is the first time I've been given an assignment where I'm expected to come up with the topic and work on it independently. I feel like I've been thrown in at the deep end."
"But knowing you, Haruki-kun, you'd feel like a fish in water, right?"
"You don't only take classes seriously, Haruki-kun. You're also always so interested in the subject that you even study tons of stuff that doesn't appear in tests."
"I've always respected that about you. I'm actually really proud."
"Just kidding. You don't really think of it as anything special yourself, so me being proud sounds kinda weird, doesn't it…?"
"Anyway, I'll be cheering you on. I'll text you again after your paper's done."
"That way, I'll be able to send something congratulatory next time. Talk to you soon."
"Mmmm… All done～!"
"Let me take a look."
Izumi, who had been sitting in front of me until now, lets out an inarticulate sound and dives onto my bed, as if recreating a scene out of an adulterous manga.
The conclusion of the paper is visible on the laptop screen, signifying an end to the arduous battle that has lasted over twenty days.
…Well, the last page looks to be in order, at least.
"I can't use my head any more～! I can't move my body any more, either～! I don't want to do anything for another mooonth～!"
"Stop swimming on my bed."
She says she can't move, but she seems as energetic as ever.
I scroll to the first page and start checking this paper that isn't mine.
"…Whoa!"
It's only the cover page and I already see something wrong.
There's no title, no cover, or even a name. It's completely blank…
"I'll start by sleeping a whole 24 hours! Then, when I wake up, I'll eat until I can't eat any more! And then, and then… What should I do about the last of my three basic needs?"
"The toilet's through that door and to your left."
"Are you implying that my last basic need is either defecation or sexual desire?"
"I think both suit you just fine."
"You mean you wouldn't mind if my moans were audible from in there?"
"Go home."
…Ah, a typo.
"Don't be so cold, Haruki～! We've been fighting it out and eating from the same pot through this twenty-day war together as comrades, haven't we?"
"We only ate out of the same pot a total of three times. And I didn't even have a choice in the matter."
Then fix up the line break here and change the font size a little… Ah, putting some emphasis on this part might work well.
"What are you talking about? You're the only one that wanted me to hand in a paper in the first place, Haruki."
"At least try to graduate, Miss University Student."
The list of references is… all finished. Alright, all that's left is to save it…
"I guess that should do it. Yeah, you've actually finished it."
"…Really?"
"I'll have to mess with the format a little, but there doesn't seem to be any problems with the content at all. Nothing that I could find, at least."
"…You're actually serious?"

"They might think that you're making leaps in your logic here and there, but these old folk tales might not have been consistent logically in the first place. You certainly showed that you've done your research, and above all, it's an interesting read."
"Wow… This is the first time you've ever praised me this much, Haruki!"
"A job well done, Izumi. And an impressive amount of effort, considering your usual self."
"Aww, yeah! Nailed it!"
"Just because I say it's a pass doesn't mean it'll guarantee you won't be held back. The professor will be grading this, not me."
"That's not all that important, really. Just having you acknowledge it already makes all the effort we've spent on it more than worthwhile, Haruki."
"Izumi…"
I suppose she sounds more like a reformed delinquent, but I still feel deeply moved by it, if only a little.
…Wait, I just totally messed up my Japanese there. How can someone be "deeply moved, if only a little"?
"Oh boy… Now that my mind's at ease, all the energy has left my body. I can't use my head anymore～ Can't move my body either～"
"I'm pretty sure you threw away all your energy and motivation well before you felt at ease."
Still, I suppose I can acknowledge her efforts this time, at least.
No matter how hard I pressured her into doing it, she couldn't have finished if she didn't have the dedication to do so herself.
…Even if her only driving force was not getting expelled.
"Hey, Haruki, let's throw a party! You still have some beer left over in your fridge, right? You know, that six-pack!"
"How do you know what I've got in my fridge? I don't even remember having that myself"
"Oh, I swiped some fish sausages from there. Don't worry, I left one for you!"
"Jeez…"
Has this girl even heard of the word "restraint"…? Well, I suppose I already know the answer to that.
I open my fridge and find a barren wasteland, devoid of any form of sustenance… Scratch that, it's actually not as bad as I'd thought it'd be.
There's that six-pack of beer she mentioned. The one fish sausage. And a pack of sliced cheese.
If I combined these with the snacks that Takeya and Io left last time, I could probably whip up a platter of canapes.
Alright, I should be able to…
"Ah…"
I glance at the clock, and the plan I haphazardly threw together disappears along with the hours that already passed by.
"What's wrong? Is your fridge cleaned out? Wanna go out and buy something, then?"
"No…"
There's only an hour left until the last train.
"Don't worry, I won't blow more than 3000 yen on snacks."
"That's not the problem here."
If we start drinking now, does she really think she'll be able to go home in an hour…?
"Fine, then! I'll split the bill with you for today! You don't see a woman who'd pay for her own celebration party everyday, now, do you? Has your impression of me improved a little?"
"Izumi…"
Now that I think of it, she did mention something about sleeping for 24 hours, didn't she? Does she really plan on staying over again today?
"All right, give me a second to get ready. Oh yeah, while we're there, why don't we get some more beer?"
…Well, I guess this was to be expected. She did produce results, and I never clearly said no to begin with.
"Izumi."
Then…
"Chuuhai, cocktails, and a few more cans of beer should do it. Ah, should we get a bottle of wine, too?"
"It's about time for you to head home."
"Ugh…"
I need to clearly say no.
"But the party…"
"The last train's going to leave soon. If we start drinking now, you won't be able to head home, just like last time."
"Oh, who cares if I go home or not～?"
"I care. You have to go home."
"But I stayed over last time, didn't I?"
"It was 1 AM back then, and it's only 11:30 PM right now."
"But I'm super tireeed～! I can't move another steeep～!"
"Weren't you all raring to head to the convenience store just now?"
"I can't move further than a thousand steeeps～!"
"Don't just change that bit. Go home."
"Why～? Why are you being so cold all of a sudden, Haruki～?"
"Um… I feel a bit bad for your parents, Izumi."
"If you're worried about that, then wasn't what happened last week already enough to apologize to them for?"
"Well, that's… Wait, nothing happened last week!"
"…So does that mean today will be different from last time, and you're planning to do something that you'll have to apologize to my parents for?"
"No. Not a chance. Absolutely not."
"…Something about that response rubs me the wrong way, but I'll let it slide. So, why can't I stay over?"
"Um, well…"
My left hand brushes against my cell phone.
The name of the person whose dozen or so new texts still lie there in wait flashes through my mind.
"If you really want to throw a party, why don't we do it at the beginning of next week, on the last day of the seminar? I'll treat you to whatever you want then."
But I can't just say that. I can't tell her the real reason.
"Ogiso… Yukina? I think that was her name."
After all, I did tell her that she didn't need to "clear up any misunderstandings."
Since I turned down Izumi's offer to patch things up, I've basically admitted that it's not her fault.
"Don't just stay over at my place or crash at the university. Actually go home. Your parents must be worried about you."
Which means that if I tell her why I'm not letting her stay over, it'll bring up the issue of whether or not she was at fault again, just like last week.
This concerns not only the events of that one week and how the two of us missed one another again, but also our current situation where we're trying to reconcile with one another.
I'd be admitting that Izumi's each and every action has an unreasonably great influence on me right now.
"I'll walk you to the station. Come on, let's go."
"Izumi… come on."
I pick up the coat that fell off her shoulders and put it on her again.
Her shoulders, drooping and without a hint of movement, are almost enough to tell me that she hasn't accepted my explanation in the slightest.
"There's no way my parents would be worried about me. They don't give a damn about what I do anyway."
The delay between my question and her answer catches me off guard, slowing down my reaction.
"…Wanna hear more?"
"…!? Ah, n-not at all."
"Sure you do～! You want to know more about why I'm so against going back home, don't you, Haruki～?"
She's at it again…
Despite looking so depressed, she suddenly peeks up at me and stares intently at my wavering eyes.
"Let's see, let's see… Oh yeah. My mother has been physically abusing me ever since I was little. My back's full of bruises and scars… Wanna see?"
"No, I'm absolutely sure you're lying. I won't tell you why, though…"
After all, you took your top off in front of me not too long ago.
There's no way I'd forget that beautiful, silky smooth back of yours so easily…
"F-Fine! I was actually sexually abused by my step-dad…"
"If that's true, then it would be okay for me to head to your place and confront your parents about this, right?"
"B-But, I have to take my living expenses and conditions afterward into account, too. If you're willing to take care of me for the rest of my life, Haruki, then I suppose…"
"If what you said was indeed the truth, I'd do everything I could to support you, using whatever means necessary."
"Ugh…"
Suing for damages, scholarships, and protecting her from possible slander from others in the event that the news spread to the public, to name a few.
I'd protect Izumi from any further wounds and do everything in my power to prevent her existing wounds from opening up again.
Because, after all…
"Sorry, that was a lie."
"Don't apologize to me, apologize to the people who have actually gone through abuse like that. Even if you're only apologizing in your heart."
The odds of losing that gamble was ridiculously low anyway.
"Oh, come on～! You know so much about me already, Haruki～ What's this? Are you that interested in me?"
"Come on, time to go. I'll listen to the rest on the way to the station."
I swear, Izumi's house is somewhat far away, sure, but does that really warrant her acting like such a brat…
"Well, that was more or less what I expected. I don't have a stepfather, and my real dad isn't around anyway."
"O-Oh?"
"I live together with my mom, you see, and we don't exactly get along with each other."
"So I pretty much never sleep at home. I either stay on campus, hit up an internet cafe, or come crash at your place."
"Don't make it sound like that last option is as common as the others. You only stayed over once."
"I only go home to get a change of clothes. And I try to never stay there for more than an hour, since if my mom happened to come home, we'd just end up arguing."
"But she's still doing the laundry for you, right?"
"The housekeeper does it. She comes over on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so I try to pick those days to go home."
What is this?
"Now then, what kind of a retort will it be this time?"
Why does it sound so unspectacular, so commonplace, almost as if I'd heard it somewhere before…
"…Well, I say that, but that's about all I really want to tell you. An undramatic tale like this usually gets boring halfway through."
No… Never mind the fact that it sounds familiar, this feeling of not wanting to give up welling inside me is why her story makes me unnecessarily uneasy.
My left hand brushes against my cell phone again.
Since I told her to not stay up too late, I should at least report the progress of my paper to her before the date changes.
No, it's not really because of a sense of obligation or anything. It's just that I have something I want to tell her. I'm yearning for a conversation, to be connected with her.
"Izumi…"
"Hm?"
Still, still…
I'm not sure if what I heard just now is the truth, a lie, or simply a misunderstanding. It was just another bunch of thoughts she blurted out on a whim.
"You know, you should really…"
However, I'm sure the last train will definitely leave if I keep listening to her.
And I won't be able to tell her to go home or anything similar when that happens.
In that case…
1. I should talk with her a little more.
2. I should tell her we should call it a day.
"It's 11:55 PM right now, and I'm about… 80% done, I think?"
"So I'm sorry. I don't think I'll be able to finish the paper today. Or rather, I'm certain that I won't."
"I'm sure I'll have to work through the night, too. I won't be able to reply to your texts for a little while. Sorry."
"We had a lot of leeway in regards to the theme of the paper, so it's certainly a piece of cake, like you said, but I might have bitten off more than I can chew."
"I ended up wanting to put this and that into my paper, and before I knew it, I'd already put a ridiculous amount of content in."
"Can you believe I'm the same guy that's always trying to tell others to act within their limits?"
"Anyway, I'll stop here for now. I'll work hard to become worthy of your congratulatory text tomorrow morning, Setsuna."
"Actually, if I don't have it finished by tomorrow, I'll probably not be able to advance to the next year."
"Good night. And tomorrow, for sure…"
"…Sorry, Setsuna."
No matter how much time passes, people always tend to ramble on and on whenever they're trying to lie, that much is a fact.
I was supposed to use these texts to bring us back together, yet I'm using them to betray Setsuna once again…
I guess I really can't stay with Setsuna…
"And now, for tonight's lovey-dovey text messages!"
"Uwahh!?"
"Ah, come on, let me see your embarrassing texts, Haruki!"
"If you know they're embarrassing, then don't peek!"
They're covered by the bath towel, but I can clearly see them swaying back and forth…
"Ah, stop trying to hide it!"
"You're the one that should be hiding something right now, Izumi!"
Why does this woman always make a joke out of all of my moments of regret and conflict?
"Ah, that felt so good. You should hurry and take a bath too, Haruki. I'll be waiting out here to toast with you."
"I'm fine, just start by yourself. I won't be drinking."
"Eeeh? Why? We finally managed to put an end to that painful battle of ours, Haruki, and you're already thinking of declaring another war?"
"I did say I'd talk with you some more, but I never said I'd do it while drinking."
"A man and woman by themselves in the middle of the night. If they're not going to drink, then isn't there only one thing left to do?"
"Yeah, which is to talk. …Don't peek, okay?"
But…
For a moment, and just a little bit… I felt like I couldn't bring myself to make Izumi go home, for whatever reason.
"It was about three years ago. Right when I was about to enter university."
"I see."
Her parents divorced right before she entered university.
"Well, I wasn't a kid anymore, so I didn't really make much of a fuss about it."
It's not really anything that rare, nor is it anything that shocking. Something you could find anywhere in the world.
"I wasn't okay with it or anything, but it's not like I was under the impression that I was being abandoned either. I wasn't that delusional."
"Yeah…"
I can't say if that's a good thing or a bad thing, but regardless, the world is still spinning, and children are still growing older.
"Actually, I'm still on pretty good terms with my dad. But I don't get to do much more besides having a meal with him once every month or so."
Izumi said she's living with her mother right now.
"On the other hand, the person who got legal custody over me is getting on my nerves more and more with each passing day."
Still, while she addresses her father properly, she seems to utilize all sorts of roundabout ways to refer to her mother.
"Every time we get together, they start arguing like crazy right in front of my eyes. It does get annoying, but sometimes I actually feel sorry for them."
"Since my dad wasn't around most of the time, I believed the tales about his supposed affairs or relationships with girls at work and whatnot."
"I see…"
"And then… after the divorce, she directed all the energy normally used to argue with her husband on me…"
"She's so annoying. Unbearably annoying. I don't want to deal with her at all anymore."
"Izumi…"
"If I come home late from a party, she spends a whole hour asking what I've been doing. If some guy calls me, she forces me to explain in detail who he is and what his relationship with me is."
The little incidents involving her mother that Izumi's telling me about just keep getting more and more twisted.
"She never had this overprotective tendency in the past, but now she practically jumps on me the instant she sees an opportunity."
"…She probably doesn't think it would have such an effect on me, but it's getting so annoying that I can't help but feel like this."
These twisted thoughts of hers have no way of straightening themselves out. They can only string together, one twisted thought onto another, and further deform beyond repair.
"And, when I think back to the divorce now, it's like no surprise at all that my dad left her."

In the end, the daughter that decided to unconcern herself with it all, and the mother who couldn't do anything other than regret her daughter's decision, formed this relationship you could find anywhere in the world.
"…It's the exact opposite in my case."
Talk about being stuck between a rock and a hard place.
"Are you on good terms with your parents, Haruki?"
"…Am I? I can't really tell, honestly. I haven't talked to them in over a year now."
"Do they live far away? Huh? But, Haruki, didn't you go to Houjou High…"
"It's about two stations away from here. I could even walk there if I wanted to."
"…So why are you living by yourself like this?"
"I happen to earn enough to rent a place for myself."
"That's not what I'm asking…"
"Then tell me. If you could earn enough money to sustain yourself, would you still stick to your current lifestyle?"
"…I guess you have a point."
"That's why even when I got accepted to Houjou High, and even when I got the highest score on a test, my parents never praised me."
"…I've never gotten any grades worthy of being praised, so I can't say I really relate to what you're saying."
"Didn't you get accepted into our university?"
"…That was more or less a miracle. Yeah, that alone was probably worthy of some overwhelming praise, but it was just around the time when my family was starting to fall apart."
"Well, that's the gist of it. Our situations started out pretty similar, but we branched off in completely different directions after that, didn't we?"
Our initial conditions were about the same, and even the feelings we harbor toward our parents are roughly identical, but the difference between how emotionally distanced we are is staggering.
"Even so, in the end, we're more or less the same. Pretty funny if you think about it, huh?"
"I'm not sure if I can bring myself to laugh at something like this, though."
But it's just as Izumi says.
It doesn't matter if it's near or far. If that distance isn't exactly what it should be, the end result would be the same.
"Which do you prefer, Haruki? Being too close together, or being too far apart?"
"Why are my only options the extremes…?"
But even so…
"But you know, doesn't 'find a happy middle ground' sound too small and too unambitious of a way of life?"
"I've been unambitious for as long as I can remember. That's why safe and practical choices were the only ones I could make."
"That's rich coming from a spoiled rich kid from Okayama."
I'm only realizing it now, but… I think I might've said too much today.
"…I really shouldn't have told you that. You're only allowed to bring that up as a joke once a month at the most, got it?"
"Heh, you're not going to ban it completely?"
"I'm simply aware that there's no point in trying to aim for the impossible."
But, I mean, what was I supposed to do?
"Should I be grateful for your kindness, or should I get mad at you for belittling me…?"
"As if you've ever been grateful to anyone for anything."
After all, this woman, who's lying on my bed and staring at me before my very eyes, has told me so much about herself already.
"As you wish. I suppose I'll get mad then. What an awful man you are, Haruki…"
"Change that to 'person,' would you? I don't remember hurting you in any way only a 'man' could."
Having elaborately explained the history of her family without hiding anything whatsoever, I'm starting to feel conscious about the slight unfairness of it all.
"So basically, you're going to do it now…?"
"Good night. I always wake up at 6:30 whether or not I have something to do, and I'm not exactly nice enough to make sure not to wake anyone else up."
Now that I think about it… When was the last time I even talked to someone about myself?
"…I haven't woken up in the 6 o'clock range in years, you know?"
"You'll be able to participate in those early morning radio calisthenics you haven't done since elementary school. Isn't that great? Then…"
"Ah, wait a second. Let me just make sure of something before you fall asleep."
If I recall correctly, I told that girl, which is why I couldn't keep it a secret from "her"…
"What do you want now…? I'm already half asleep."
"You're too good at falling asleep…"
"You have ten seconds. I'll pass out if you take any longer."
"Well, you know, the paper's done… So I don't really have a reason to keep coming here anymore."
Ah… Are those days from three years ago coming back to me yet again?
"…But can I still come and hang out?"
"…Just make sure to leave on time next time."
I must have cleared countless unthinkable milestones back in those days.
"Don't worry, I'll be on time. I'll be gone by the time the first train arrives."
"Actually, just don't come again."
When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?
In the end…
Even though I made such a firm declaration, it was already noon by the time Izumi and I managed to wake up.
Mostly because her wanting to "make sure of something" ended up leading us into reminiscing about our childhoods.

By the time I could finally close my eyes after making sure Izumi was asleep as well, the winter sky had already been lit up by the morning sun. …And it was already far past the time I usually wake up.

Izumi lazed around in my room some more after that, eating the lunch I made and even stealing some of my share, too. It wasn't until the sky had been soaked in crimson that she finally left my apartment.
Thanks to Izumi, my long-awaited day off came to an end before I knew it.
Her cheerful parting words of "what a valuable waste of time that was" felt utterly superficial. I wonder if I'll ever be able to feel the same way?
"Hey, Mom? You sent me a text yesterday, right? What's up?"
"…Um, I'm at Minami-Suetsugu right now, so it'll probably be an hour before I get there."
"Okay, got it. We'll meet at the usual place in an hour, okay?"
"But seriously, what's the occasion? It's not every day that you take me out for dinner. Did something nice happen?"
"How am I doing? Well, I'm… Oh yeah, I should thank you, Mom."
"…Thanks for being a part of my little story."
"Okay, then just as you requested… Congratulations, Kitahara Haruki-kun!"
"Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."
"And when he saw the wine I prepared in my room, he even said that I was going way overboard with a face of complete shock."
"Well, enough about that. I guess we can start enjoying winter break now without having to worry, huh?"
"Do you have any plans for the break, Haruki-kun? Are you going to be working part-time like always?"
"I remember you saying before that Christmas and New Year's are always great for making money since most people aren't working."
"Is it the same this year, too? Have you thought about just relaxing through the break at all?"
"…I don't really mean anything by that. I'm just a little curious, that's all."
"Yep, no other hidden intentions at all."
"…I'm currently finishing my first glass and am about to pour my second～"
"Thanks for the congratulatory text."
"I still have finals in the second term, but since I already have the credits I need, I'm more or less guaranteed to move on to my fourth year now."
"The paper was quite a challenge, but it helped me get some insight on how to tackle my graduation thesis, so even though it was quite the struggle, I managed to get something out of it after all."
"But more importantly, shouldn't you slow down a little, Setsuna?"
"Didn't you use to get drunk after just a single glass of wine? You do plan on waking up tomorrow, right?"
"Sorry, Professor～! I don't have an answer to that question yeeet～"
"Time for the third～"
"I told you you'd get drunk! Your writing is all over the place, you know?"
"Stop drinking already, okay? I don't want to be responsible for any other weird things you might end up writing."
"What do you mean, weird? Is it really strange of me to ask about your winter holiday plans, Haruki-kun?"
"I just thought that if you don't take part in some more lively events like skiing or shrine-visiting once in a while, you'll go senile in no time, Haruki-kun～"
"Didn't you say you didn't mean anything when you asked that?"
"You used 'didn't' twice there, you know? Doesn't that sound weird, Haruki-kun? And here I thought you were a literature student～"
"Gah, stop being so picky!"
"Gah, stop being so picky!"
"Ahaha… You got angry! Haruki-kun got mad while trying to lecture me～ This is so fun～"
"I'm not mad!"
"I'm not mad! You should go to sleep soon, Setsuna. You won't be able to wake up otherwise, you know?"
"Yeah. I feel all woozy right now～ I even promised to go shopping with my mom in the morning, too."
"Hey, uh… Should I give you a call and wake you up in the morning?"
"Please do!"
"G-Good morning!"
"…Were you really asleep up until now?"
And so…
Hearing Setsuna's voice for the first time after an entire week is so… How should I put it…?
I'm probably feeling the same things she is right now. Nostalgia, joy… and just a touch of pain.
